title: The Rough Escarpment
premise: Coral Ashgrove, a salvage diver drowning in debt, takes one last job on a wreck the navy quietly forbids anyone to touch, and finds among the rust a compass that shouldn't exist. A dying prospector trades her a map to a hidden cache in exchange for a promise she barely understands, and suddenly the navy, a salvage syndicate, and the prospector's own family are all hunting the same coordinates. With monsoon season closing in and her boat taking on water, Coral must trust a stranger named Wren Vale who may be working for the other side. In the end Coral reaches the cache first, discovers it holds proof of the navy's buried crime rather than treasure, and must choose between selling it for her freedom or exposing the truth at the cost of everything she's built.
about_author: Quentin Ashgrove is the pen name of a former maritime surveyor who spent six years mapping wrecks along contested coastlines before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about people whose livelihoods depend on staying unnoticed by powerful institutions.

chapters.title: Salt Debt
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Diving a sunken freighter off a coast the navy patrols too carefully, Coral salvages enough brass to cover half her debt to the Harrow syndicate. The emotional beat is weary defiance: she's good at surviving small, and she tells herself that's enough.

chapters.title: The Wreck Nobody Names
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Her handler offers triple pay for a dive on an unlisted wreck inside a restricted zone. Below, past a sealed compartment, she finds a brass compass with no needle—only a ring of numbers. Fear and greed war in her as she pockets it instead of reporting it.

chapters.title: A Stranger on the Pier
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren Vale, posing as a marine insurance clerk, watches Coral dock and reports her position to someone over a cracked radio. The beat is complicity: Wren believes they're doing necessary work, and lies to themselves about what 'necessary' means.

chapters.title: The Prospector's Bargain
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. An old prospector named Ede Latch finds Coral bleeding from a bar fight and patches her up. Dying, he trades her a hand-drawn map to a coastal cache for a promise: deliver it to his daughter, or burn it. Coral accepts mostly because refusing feels impossible.

chapters.title: Numbers That Point Nowhere
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At home, Coral realizes the compass's number-ring matches markings on Ede's map—the map and compass are halves of one mechanism. Excitement curdles into dread when she spots a navy launch idling beyond the breakwater, watching her boat.

chapters.title: Harrow Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Syndicate enforcer Bram Harrow visits, having heard about her restricted-zone job. He offers to forgive her debt if she hands over whatever she lifted. Coral lies smoothly and hates how easily lying has become her native language.

chapters.title: Cutting Loose
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral slips harbor at dawn with the map, compass, and a hull already weeping at a seam. The beat is exhilarating escape shadowed by grief—she's leaving behind the only life, shabby as it was, that she knew how to live.

chapters.title: The Stranger Aboard
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren intercepts Coral mid-channel, claiming their own boat was stolen and begging passage. Coral, suspicious but short-handed before the monsoon, grudgingly agrees. Wren's private beat: guilt sharpening into something dangerously like genuine affection.

chapters.title: First Squall
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A squall forces them to run the boat hard; Coral nearly loses the compass overboard and Wren catches it—an act that could be loyalty or theft. Forced teamwork cracks open first real conversation, and mutual suspicion becomes reluctant respect.

chapters.title: The Navy's Shadow
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A patrol cutter shadows them for hours before peeling away. Coral deciphers more of the map and understands the cache sits inside old naval territory—and that Ede knew exactly what he was handing her. The beat is the vertigo of realizing you were chosen as a weapon.

chapters.title: What Wren Knows
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren radios a coded update, then destroys the radio, unable to send Coral's location after all. Split loyalties ache: the mission was supposed to be simple, and Coral keeps being a person instead of a target.

chapters.title: The Leaking Hold
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The hull seam fails properly; they pump through the night and beach on a nameless cay. Stranded together, Coral finds Wren's hidden transmitter. The beat is cold betrayal—but Coral doesn't confront them yet, deciding information is worth more than confrontation.

chapters.title: Ede's Daughter
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. On the cay they find Sera Latch, Ede's daughter, living rough and armed. Sera reveals the cache contains evidence of a navy cover-up—a sunk refugee ship, officially never there. Coral's promise transforms from errand into moral weight.

chapters.title: Three-Way Standoff
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Bram Harrow's fast boat arrives, followed by the navy cutter. Sera, Coral, and a wavering Wren hide the evidence canister while the two forces argue over jurisdiction. The beat is terror under discipline: everyone smiling while measuring each other for coffins.

chapters.title: The Deal Offered
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Harrow privately offers Coral full debt forgiveness plus passage anywhere—if she gives him the canister and lets Wren take the fall as a spy. Coral asks for a night to decide, then finally confronts Wren, who confesses everything except the one thing that matters: why they stayed.

chapters.title: Monsoon Rising
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The storm front arrives early, blackening the horizon. All parties are trapped on the cay together. Coral makes her choice in secret, sealing the canister into the boat's bilge where only a diver would ever find it. The beat is grim resolve.

chapters.title: Through the Eye
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral, Wren, and Sera make a desperate midnight run through the monsoon's eye toward the cache site itself, betting the storm will blind both pursuers. The boat nearly breaks apart; Wren saves Coral's life openly now, choosing a side at last.

chapters.title: The Cache
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Diving the flooded cistern at the map's coordinates, Coral opens the cache: logs, photographs, and a passenger manifest proving the navy sank a ship full of civilians and called it a training accident. Surfacing, she finds Harrow waiting on the rocks with a gun.

chapters.title: Bargaining with Guns
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Harrow demands the evidence; the navy cutter closes in. Wren turns their insider knowledge against both sides, feeding the navy false coordinates and triggering a standoff that lets Coral slip underwater with the canister. The beat is sacrifice offered without asking permission.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Climax. Cornered between Harrow and the surf, Coral dives deep and hides the canister in the wreck of the refugee ship itself—letting the dead guard the truth. Harrow, unwilling to explain his presence to arriving navy officers, retreats. Coral surfaces empty-handed and free.

chapters.title: The Promise Kept
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Aftermath: Coral delivers Ede's message to Sera—not the map, but the truth of what her father died protecting. Wren, officially a deserter now, chooses to stay with Coral rather than return to handlers who'll disavow them. Quiet, hard-won tenderness.

chapters.title: The Rough Escarpment
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Months later, Coral and Wren work honest wrecks under new names while anonymously leaked documents begin unraveling the navy's cover-up far away. Standing on the escarpment above the bay, Coral reflects that survival cost her everything except the things that mattered. Hope, earned the hard way.
